text:
Write the main text for my sales page. I'm a bookkeeper and I work only with hair and nail salons. I do monthly books, payroll for up to 10 staff, and sales tax filing.

What's true:
- I have 31 salon clients. 2 left last year, both because they sold their salons.
- I charge $199 a month. Until January it was $149, and I raised it for everyone, including existing clients.
- I close each month's books by the 10th of the next month. I missed that date 3 times last year.
- Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because the books came in clean. One said she saved $800.
- I'm one person. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays.
- The first call is free and takes 20 minutes.

Keep it to about 350 words, with a button at the end to book the call.

Before I draft, here's the argument the page will make. Please correct anything that's wrong.

- **Claim:** If you own a salon, hand me your books, payroll and sales tax for $199 a month.
- **Grounds:** You work only with salons and have 31 of them. No client left last year for any reason except selling their salon, even after a $50 price rise. 9 clients paid their accountant less at tax time, and one saved $800.
- **Link:** A bookkeeper who only does salons, and whom salon owners stay with, will get your books right and save you money at tax time.
- **What a reader will push back on:** the price ("$199 when it used to be $149?"), being one person ("what if you're unavailable?"), and timing ("will my books actually be done?"). The page should answer each of these directly. I'd rather state the 3 missed close dates than hide them.

A few questions. Each answer will change what goes on the page:

1. **What do you handle that a general bookkeeper gets wrong with salons?** For example: tips, booth renters versus employees, commission pay, or retail product sales. One or two concrete examples are what make "salons only" worth paying for.
2. **The 3 missed close dates:** were these 3 months where everyone's books were late, or 3 single client-months out of about 370? What caused them, and did you change anything afterwards? Is there anything you'll commit to if you're late?
3. **The price rise:** did anyone leave over it? From what you've told me, no one did, but I want to confirm before I say so. Also, what would a salon owner otherwise pay for the same work, whether that's another bookkeeper, a payroll service or doing it themselves?
4. **Being one person:** which days and hours are you reachable, and how quickly do you usually reply? I can turn "closed Sundays and Mondays" into a plus, since that's when salons close too, but only if it's true for you.
5. **The $800 client:** can I quote her by first name and salon, or should she stay anonymous?
6. **Anything a new client will find out later:** a setup or catch-up fee for messy books, a minimum contract, how to cancel, or what happens with more than 10 staff. Who signs the page (your name or business name), and what should the button say?

Answer whichever you can. I'll leave out anything you don't know rather than guess.

1. I managed a hair salon for 6 years before I became a bookkeeper. I don't have specific examples ready beyond that.

2. I don't know the breakdown or the cause offhand. Since January: if I miss the 10th, that month's fee is free.

3. Nobody left over the price. The only 2 who left sold their salons. I raised it because I added payroll for up to 10 staff, which I didn't do before. I don't know what others charge.

4. Calls are Tuesday to Saturday. I don't have set hours or a usual reply time to give you.

5. I don't know yet if she'd be OK being named, so keep her anonymous.

6. No contract. Clients can stop with 30 days' notice. I don't do income tax returns. Their own accountant or tax preparer keeps doing those and gets clean books from me. I can only take about 5 new clients this year. I don't know about a setup fee or what happens over 10 staff. Sign it Carla Benson, Chair and Ledger. The button goes to my calendar. Use whatever wording you think works.

<final_document>
# Bookkeeping for hair and nail salons, from someone who ran one

I'm Carla Benson. Before I became a bookkeeper, I managed a hair salon for six years. Now I work only with hair and nail salons, and I have 31 of them as clients.

**For $199 a month, you get:**

- Monthly books, closed by the 10th of the following month
- Payroll for up to 10 staff
- Sales tax filing

## Clean books cost less at tax time

I don't do income tax returns. Your accountant or tax preparer keeps doing those. What changes is what they get from me: books that are already right.

Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because their books came in clean. One of them saved $800.

## Salon owners stay

Two clients left last year, and both had sold their salons.

In January I raised my price from $149 to $199 for every client, including the ones who'd been with me for years. I raised it because I added payroll for up to 10 staff, which I didn't offer before. Nobody left over the new price.

## If I'm late, you don't pay

I missed the 10th three times last year. Since January, any month I miss it is free.

## It's just me

When you call, you get me every time. I take calls Tuesday to Saturday, but not on Sundays or Mondays.

Because there's only one of me, I can take on about five new clients this year.

## No contract

If it isn't working for you, give me 30 days' notice and stop.

## Start with a 20-minute call

The first call is free. Tell me about your salon, and we'll see whether I'm the right fit.

**[ Book your free 20-minute call ]**

Carla Benson
Chair and Ledger
</final_document>

The page is about 300 words. Some things to check before it goes live:

- **"About five new clients this year":** since it's mid-November, a reader may take "this year" to mean only six weeks are left. If you meant 2027, change it to "in 2027" or "next year."
- **Left out:** setup fees and pricing for more than 10 staff, because you didn't know the answers. People will ask about both on the call, so it's worth deciding before then.
- **The three missed dates:** I stated them plainly next to the free-month promise, because the promise is the answer to them. If you later find out they were three single client-months rather than three whole months, saying so would make the page stronger.
